clue.text: Old vehicle's trim pocketed by flier

indicators.note: being pocketed by something means being held inside it, so the trim goes within the flier

parts.note: a jay is a bird, so a flier
to lop is to trim or cut back

explanation.surface: Someone's old banger has had its trim swallowed up by a passing bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' looks like a pilot or aircraft; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalopy is a dilapidated old motor car, a decrepit vehicle.

clue.text: In summer month, right to make soup

indicators.note: In places the right inside the summer month

parts.note: June is a summer month in the northern hemisphere
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A June recipe for making soup properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' here is the legal sense, a claim on property, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Julienne is a clear soup containing thin strips of vegetables.

clue.text: Lily's position?

parts.note: a cross-legged yoga pose named after the water lily, read as a posture adopted by the flower

explanation.surface: Asks where a woman named Lily stands, or what pose she takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a name; it is the flower, which gives its name to a yoga posture.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, and the lotus position is a cross-legged yoga pose.

clue.text: Ward got peer in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means in a mess, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A young charge has landed a nobleman in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges GOT PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone under the guidance and protection of a patron, like a ward.

clue.text: Cheap American couple snapped

parts.note: a couple is two
snapped, as a dog does, means bit

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted pair from the States lost their tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' belongs to the definition: the term is US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is US slang for worthless or shoddy, from the old quarter-dollar coin.

clue.text: Cleaner with wooden thumb, oddly?

parts.note: ash is a hardwood, so something wooden may be ash

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters, first third and fifth, of thumb

explanation.surface: A cleaner whose thumb is strangely made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' picks TUB from THUMB. The question mark flags that this cleaner is a container, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A washtub is a tub used for washing clothes, so a cleaning vessel.

clue.text: Scotsman raised in TV age could be picture producer

indicators.note: in places the raised Scotsman inside the TV age

parts.note: the box is slang for television, so a TV age is a box era

indicators.note: in a down light, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Mac is a familiar term for a Scotsman, from the surname prefix

explanation.surface: A Scot brought up in the television era might become a photographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' is British slang for television; 'raised' reverses because this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A box camera is a simple early camera, a device that produces photographs.

clue.text: Drier about middle of April: gardener might need this

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the drier goes round the centre letter

parts.note: a towel is something you dry yourself with

indicators.note: middle of takes the centre letter of April

explanation.surface: Dry weather around mid-April, when gardeners need their tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes R from APRIL; 'about' wraps TOWEL around it. 'Drier' looks like weather; it is a towel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for digging, used constantly in gardening.

clue.text: Place stripper removed item of footwear

indicators.note: removed here means moved again, so the letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: A spot where a stripper took off a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges PLACE STRIPPER; read it as re-moved.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft indoor shoe, traditionally made of carpet-like fabric.

clue.text: More than enough to help working artist

indicators.note: working here means being worked into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An offer of assistance to a busy painter is more than generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges TO HELP into PLETHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or superabundance of something.

clue.text: Church officer attacked violently, unknown admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the unknown goes inside the phrase for attacked

parts.note: set on means attacked violently
X is the usual algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A church official was assaulted, with an unidentified assailant confessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' puts X inside SET ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a parish official who looks after the church building and graveyard.

clue.text: Deity revealed by canal backing up

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the canal's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea

explanation.surface: A god appears when traffic on a waterway backs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing up' turns SUEZ around.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus is the king of the gods in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Held forth on person living abroad facing one terrible date

parts.note: an expat is someone living outside their own country
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of date are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone lectured on an emigrant who has an awful date in prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject.

clue.text: Ban peace cult out of hand? It's not on!

indicators.note: out of hand means out of control, so these letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A call to outlaw a peace cult that has got out of control, deemed intolerable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of hand' rearranges BAN PEACE CULT.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not on' is British idiom for not acceptable or not allowed.

clue.text: American river crossed by container vessel

indicators.note: crossed by means having something lie across it, so the container takes the pieces within it

parts.note: a can is a container
the Tamar is a river on the Devon-Cornwall border

explanation.surface: An American river ferry crossing, by container ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is not American: 'American' gives a lone letter, and the river divides the English counties of Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls.

clue.text: Got hold of mostly free wine

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for free is dropped

parts.note: to acquit is to free from a charge
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: Someone obtained wine that came almost for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the T from ACQUIT, leaving ACQUI.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain or gain possession of it.

clue.text: Bookkeeper's test of equilibrium?

parts.note: an accounts check that debits and credits match, read as a trial of balance

explanation.surface: A query about how an accountant checks the books agree.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a trial is a test and balance is equilibrium.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookkeeping, this list of all ledger accounts checks that debit totals equal credit totals.

clue.text: Book Russian to sit on throne occasionally

indicators.note: in a down light, sitting on means placed above, so the Russian comes first

parts.note: Ivan is a typical Russian name, standing for a Russian

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of throne

explanation.surface: Booking a Russian to take the throne now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sit on' works because this is a down light: the Russian sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is Sir Walter Scott's historical novel.

clue.text: Fish and beer with married woman

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a wife is a married woman

explanation.surface: A pub supper of fish and beer with one's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alewife is a North American herring-like fish.

clue.text: Commercial opening just before Christmas

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A shop advert launched just ahead of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the church season of the four weeks leading up to Christmas.

clue.text: What might bring a lump to one's throat

definitions.text: What might bring a lump to one's throat

parts.words: What might bring a lump to one's throat
parts.note: a lump in the throat is usually emotion, but here it is the physical bulge of the larynx

explanation.surface: Something moving enough to make you choke up.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a sentimental moment; the answer is the literal lump in the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the visible bulge of cartilage at the front of the neck, named after the forbidden fruit.

clue.text: Spell in ring, but outside

indicators.note: the word but stands outside, enclosing the ring

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A short time in the boxing ring, but out of it too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps BUT around O; 'in' links the two. The surface pushes 'Spell in ring' as a boxing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a short period or spell of activity or illness.

clue.text: Herb's lab is vandalised

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are broken and reordered

explanation.surface: A laboratory has been wrecked, and a man called Herb is blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges LAB IS; 'Herb' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic culinary plant used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Explore south-eastern part of church?

parts.note: an arch is a structural part of a church

explanation.surface: An invitation to look around one corner of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To search is to explore or look through somewhere thoroughly.

clue.text: One sent on an errand as misery develops

indicators.note: develops means changes and grows into something else, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A messenger sets off on a job as gloom sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' rearranges AS MISERY.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an envoy or messenger sent on a mission.

clue.text: Vessel that's well-filled

parts.note: a ship whose hold is filled up with oil, or a heavy drinker who is well tanked up

explanation.surface: A boat carrying a full load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-filled' also hints at someone tanked up, slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This ship carries liquid cargo such as oil in bulk tanks.

clue.text: Well now, that's better

definitions.meaning: restored to health at present, cured
said of something improved after treatment, mended

explanation.surface: A soothing exclamation of relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cured of illness is well again and has got better.
